collectionMetadata.name: THE LIVING INDEX
collectionMetadata.description: A museum-grade digital collection framework for independent collectors, antiquarians, and private archivists. Maintained under strict conservational standards and dual-surface ledger telemetry.
collectionMetadata.curatorialStatement: The Living Index establishes an empirical custody protocol for physical heritage. Every specimen catalogued herein is bound to its accession code, calibrated microclimate tolerances, and verifiable provenance chain. We reject digital ephemeralization in favor of dense scholarly accountability.

items.title: Breguet No. 160 Grand Complication ('Marie-Antoinette')
items.medium: 18k gold, sapphire crystal, platinum and blued-steel train, 82 natural rubies
items.mediumSubstrate: 18-karat yellow gold case, rock crystal dials, blued-steel screws, natural ruby endstones

storageMicroclimate.atmosphericEnvironment: Nitrogen-purged anaerobic casing, zero ambient sulfides

items.provenanceText: Commissioned in 1783 for Queen Marie-Antoinette by an officer of the Garde du Corps; completed in 1827 by Abraham-Louis Breguet's son Antoine-Louis Breguet; collection of Sir David Lionel Salomons, 1925; L.A. Mayer Museum for Islamic Art, Jerusalem; accessioned to Living Index Trust custody 2012.

provenanceChain.holder: Officer of the French Garde du Corps (Anonymous)
provenanceChain.notes: Commission stipulated every complication known to horology with no time or cost ceiling.
Completed 34 years after the death of Marie-Antoinette and 4 years after Abraham-Louis Breguet's death.
Recorded in Salomons Breguet Monograph as masterwork No. 160.
Complete mechanical disassembly and stabilization documented in conservatorial folio.

spectralImaging.xrfAnalysis: Gold 75.2% Au, 16.1% Ag, 8.7% Cu alloy profile

items.curatorialNotes: Regarded as the pinnacle of 18th-century horological engineering. Features perpetual calendar, equation of time, jumping hours, minute repeater, bimetallic thermometer, and independent central seconds. Escapement operates on natural ruby cylinder with shock-absorbing pare-chute suspension.

items.title: HMS Beagle Marine Chronometer (Thomas Earnshaw No. 509)
items.medium: Lacquered brass, spring detent escapement, compensated bimetallic balance, silvered dial
items.mediumSubstrate: Cast gunmetal brass, hardened blued-steel helical balance spring, English oak gimbal box

storageMicroclimate.atmosphericEnvironment: Filtered inert nitrogen micro-chamber, silica-gel desiccated buffer

items.provenanceText: Manufactured by Thomas Earnshaw, 119 High Holborn, London; purchased by the British Board of Longitude; assigned to Admiralty Hydrographic Department; embarked on HMS Beagle second surveying voyage (1831–1836) under Captain Robert FitzRoy carrying naturalist Charles Darwin; British Museum transfer.

provenanceChain.notes: Spring detent escapement numbered 509 engraved on backplate.
One of 22 marine chronometers carried on the Beagle to establish a global chain of longitude meridians.
Transferred under Admiralty Scientific Instrument Relinquishment Act.
Escapement stabilized without abrasive polishing; original oil residues preserved for spectrographic analysis.

spectralImaging.xrfAnalysis: Brass alloy: 68.4% Cu, 31.2% Zn, trace Pb 0.4%

items.curatorialNotes: Earnshaw's spring detent revolutionized navigational precision. During the five-year circumnavigation of HMS Beagle, No. 509 maintained a mean daily rate variance under 0.18 seconds, anchoring the longitude calculations that underpinned Darwin's geographic observations.
items.rightsStatement: British Museum / Wikimedia Commons Public Domain

items.title: Besler: Hortus Eystettensis (Prince-Bishop's Eichstätt Florilegium)
items.medium: Hand-colored copperplate engraving on handmade rag paper, pigskin binding
items.mediumSubstrate: 100% linen rag laid paper with Bishop's crest watermark, copperplate intaglio inks, gum arabic mineral pigments

storageMicroclimate.atmosphericEnvironment: UV filtered zero-ozone atmosphere, archival deacidified tissue interleaves

items.provenanceText: Commissioned by Prince-Bishop Johann Konrad von Gemmingen of Eichstätt, Bavaria; executed by apothecary-botanist Basilius Besler and team of Nuremberg engravers; Willibaldsburg Castle library; rescued during Thirty Years' War (1634); private Bavarian collection; acquired 2018.

provenanceChain.holder: Johann Konrad von Gemmingen, Prince-Bishop of Eichstätt
provenanceChain.notes: Deluxe colored edition of 367 plates depicting 1,084 species cultivated in the eight episcopal terrace gardens.
Sheltered from Swedish sack of Willibaldsburg Castle during Thirty Years' War.
Deacidified buffer applied to margins; pigskin tooling cleaned with anhydrous leather dressing.

spectralImaging.xrfAnalysis: Pigment scan: Malachite green, Vermilion (HgS), Azurite blue, Orpiment (As2S3)

items.curatorialNotes: The first great botanical work to break from medieval medicinal pharmacopoeia in favor of pure aesthetic and morphological representation. The folio represents the four seasons in garden horticulture, executed with uncompromising botanical veracity before the invention of modern Linnaean taxonomy.

items.title: Pierre-Joseph Redouté: Les Liliacées (Dalmatian Iris, Plate 366)
items.medium: Stipple engraving printed in color and finished by hand with watercolor on wove paper
items.mediumSubstrate: J. Whatman heavyweight wove rag paper, hand-ground organic watercolors, stipple intaglio plate impression

storageMicroclimate.atmosphericEnvironment: Encapsulated in Melinex 516 archival polyester sleeve, acid-free museum rag mat

items.provenanceText: Patronage of Empress Joséphine Bonaparte at Château de Malmaison; botanical descriptions by Augustin Pyramus de Candolle; printed by Didot Jeune, Paris; collection of the Duke of Luynes, Château de Dampierre; acquired by private treaty 2019.

provenanceChain.notes: Joséphine commissioned Redouté to record the rare bulbous monocotyledons assembled in her Malmaison greenhouses.
Maintained in dark folio cabinet with minimal daylight exposure, ensuring extraordinary pigment saturation.
Verified by spectral pigment analysis; complete absence of foxing or paper acidification.

spectralImaging.xrfAnalysis: Pigment scan: Natural indigo and Prussian blue blend; gum tragacanth glaze confirmed

items.curatorialNotes: Redouté perfected stipple engraving—using tiny copper points instead of lines—enabling delicate tonal gradations and botanical transparency. Plate 366 (Iris pallida) captures the waxy silver bloom on the lanceolate foliage and the velvety falls of the perianth with unmatched botanical fidelity.
items.rightsStatement: Google Art Project / Wikimedia Commons Public Domain

items.title: Seymchan Pallasite Meteorite (Polished Core Slice)
items.medium: Extraterrestrial olivine crystals suspended in nickel-iron kamacite/taenite matrix
items.mediumSubstrate: Pallasite (Main Group PMG-anomalous), Kamacite (α-Fe,Ni), Taenite (γ-Fe,Ni), Schreibersite, Forsteritic Olivine

storageMicroclimate.atmosphericEnvironment: Ultra-low moisture desiccator chamber, continuous nitrogen backfill to prevent chloride corrosion

items.provenanceText: Discovered in June 1967 in the bed of the Hekandue River, Magadan District, Soviet Union, by geologist F. A. Mednikov; main mass deposited with Academy of Sciences of the USSR, Moscow; secondary pallasitic section cut and polished at Vernadsky Institute; accessioned 2016.

provenanceChain.holder: F. A. Mednikov / Soviet Geological Expedition
provenanceChain.notes: Initial 272.3 kg mass discovered in dried riverbed; originally classified as octahedrite until silicate-bearing zones found.

provenanceChain.holder: Vernadsky Institute of Geochemistry and Analytical Chemistry
provenanceChain.notes: Sectioned with diamond wire saw under oil bath to avoid oxidation of olivine crystal faces.
Treated with anhydrous isopropyl alcohol dewatering bath and sealed in passivated desiccated envelope.

spectralImaging.xrfAnalysis: Ni 9.15%, Ir 19.0 ppm, Ga 24.6 ppm, Ge 68.3 ppm (Kamacite band Widmanstätten pattern)

items.curatorialNotes: Pallasites represent the boundary zone between the molten iron core and the silicate mantle of a differentiated asteroid obliterated during early solar system accretion. The golden olivine gems in this section exhibit exceptional gem-quality transparency with no terrestrial shock fracturing.

items.title: Badakhshan Ultramarine Lapis Lazuli Monolith
items.medium: Natural Lazurite silicate rock with Calcite veins and Pyrite cubic crystal inclusions
items.mediumSubstrate: (Na,Ca)8[(S,Cl,SO4,OH)2|(Al6Si6O24)] tectosilicate, contact metamorphic marble host rock

storageMicroclimate.atmosphericEnvironment: Dust-free filtered air, ambient pressure, vibration-damped plinth

items.provenanceText: Extracted from the ancient Sar-e-Sang deposits, Kokcha River Valley, Badakhshan Province, Afghanistan; transported via Kabul caravan routes to Peshawar; acquired by British Raj mineralogical survey; Geological Museum London collection; transfer to private registry 2011.

provenanceChain.notes: Mined by ancient fire-setting method in deep tunnel workings known continuously since the 4th millennium BCE.

provenanceChain.holder: Geological Survey of India / London Office
provenanceChain.notes: Catalogued as benchmark reference for true Afghan ultramarine before synthetic French ultramarine dominance.
Surface stabilized; crystalline pyrite inclusions verified under petrographic microscopy.

spectralImaging.xrfAnalysis: Raman spectroscopy confirms trisulfur radical anion (S3-) chromophore; FeS2 pyrite crystals intact

items.curatorialNotes: The Kokcha Valley is the legendary historical source of genuine lapis lazuli used across Pharaonic funerary masks, Renaissance tempera illuminations, and Vermeer's glazes. This specimen exhibits the intense royal deep ultramarine blue matrix sprinkled with brassy pyrite stars and stark white calcite fractures.

items.title: Terra Nova off Cape Evans with Capsizing Iceberg (Herbert Ponting)
items.medium: Gelatin silver carbon-toned glass plate contact print on fiber-base paper
items.mediumSubstrate: Baryta-coated heavy rag fiber paper, silver gelatin emulsion, toned with platinum-gold salts

storageMicroclimate.atmosphericEnvironment: Dark cold storage vault, acid-free rag matting, inert polyester enclosures

items.provenanceText: Photographed by Herbert Ponting, official camera artist to the British Antarctic Expedition (1910–1913) under Captain Robert Falcon Scott; developed on site at Cape Evans hut darkroom; returned to London 1912; Fine Art Society exhibition print, London, 1914; acquired 2015.

provenanceChain.notes: Exposed on a 10×8-inch plate glass negative inside Ponting's cramped darkroom cubicle during the freeze-up.
Printed under Ponting's direct supervision to raise funds for the Scott Memorial Trust.
Surface silver mirroring stabilized with micro-crystalline wax treatment; cold storage chain uninterrupted.

spectralImaging.xrfAnalysis: Silver image particles with traces of gold toning salts; zero sulfurous atmospheric tarnishing

items.curatorialNotes: Herbert Ponting was the first professional photographer attached to an Antarctic expedition. This dramatic frame captures the expedition barque Terra Nova framed by the arched grotto of a collapsing iceberg in McMurdo Sound. Ponting noted that moments after this exposure, the berg violently overturned, nearly engulfing the expedition's boat.
items.rightsStatement: Royal Geographical Society / Wikimedia Commons Public Domain

items.title: Endurance Trapped in the Weddell Sea Pack Ice (Frank Hurley)
items.medium: Paget plate flashlit silver bromide contact print with hand-toned highlights
items.mediumSubstrate: Imperial dry plate silver bromide emulsion on glass substrate, contact printed on Ilford bromide paper

storageMicroclimate.atmosphericEnvironment: Individual anodized aluminum archival cassette with desiccated zeolites

items.provenanceText: Photographed by James Francis 'Frank' Hurley, official photographer to Sir Ernest Shackleton's Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition (1914–1917); salvaged during the sinking of the Endurance from the submerged hold; cached in lead canisters on the ice pack; Mitchell Library, Sydney; private acquisition 2021.

provenanceChain.notes: Illuminated using twenty synchronized magnesium flash flares arranged around the pressure ice ridges.

provenanceChain.location: Ocean Camp, Weddell Sea Ice Floe
provenanceChain.notes: Hurley dove into waist-deep icy water in the sinking wreck to retrieve the sealed tin boxes containing 120 selected glass plates; remaining 400 plates smashed on the ice to prevent excess weight.
Emulsion edge frilling stabilized under controlled low-temperature consolidation.

spectralImaging.xrfAnalysis: Magnesium burn residue trace in emulsion border; silver bromide image structure verified

items.curatorialNotes: Taken during the long polar night as the three-masted barquentine Endurance was subjected to crushing rafted ice pressure. Hurley rigged electrical wires in sub-zero blizzards to ignite flash charges simultaneously. The resulting image reveals the ghost-like rigging encrusted in rime ice amidst towering pressure seracs.
items.rightsStatement: State Library of NSW / Wikimedia Commons Public Domain
